case.title: A new CAF control appears as a new column, with no code change

steps.text: Read every active CAF control, ordered by name — the widget's own ordering.
Open the portal compliance grid and read its column headers.
screenshots: C:\Users\patel\Documents\ServiceNow Work Project Docs\Personal AI Assisted\dev281754 CAF App Reyan\testing\automation\evidence\TC-SN-069\02-portal-grid-columns.png

steps.text: Compare the control names against the column headers.

rows.leading_attribute_columns: Critical Business Application / Service Category / Overall Conformance Status

observations: Columns are rendered in name order: true. The widget sorts with orderBy('name'), so a new control lands alphabetically rather than at the end of the grid.

Mechanism confirmed from the widget source: columns come from a GlideRecord over caf_conformance_type filtered active=true, keyed by control NAME. The superseded sys_choice query it replaced is still present, commented out — the dynamic behaviour was a deliberate migration.

DIVERGENCE: the Salesforce LWC derives its columns from request data, not from a control table, so a control with no requests gets an N/A column here and NO column in Salesforce. Sync Health cannot report that, because the control table is not mirrored. See TC-INT-049.
Part B of this case — insert a control and watch a seventh column appear — is a WRITE that leaves a permanent column on the demo grid. Not executed here; it needs explicit approval.
expected: The portal grid's control columns equal the active rows of caf_conformance_type exactly, in name order.
No hard-coded control list exists anywhere in the widget — the column set is bound to the data.
The filter panel above the grid carries one dropdown per control, from the same array.
actual: 6 active control(s); 6 appear as grid columns with none missing.
case.verdictReason: All 6 active controls are bound to grid columns. The column set is data-driven, not hard-coded. Causation still to be proven by Part B.
